source.precedence: User follow-up retains Conkeldurr for Persist and assigns Zygarde to System. Later requests assign builder/configurer pairs to Account, Environment, Build, Deploy, Model and Console. User follow-up assigns Puller polling, subscriptions and reconciliation to the Deploy product; keep subscriber state separate from its stateless run API. The 2026-10-07 request adds Documentation as a distinct product, superseding the earlier API documentation exclusion. Require the engineering and React/TypeScript/tRPC application skills; keep Site and Document separate and unassigned. The latest Account boundary correction keeps AWS account identity, keys, records, provisioning and bootstrap manifests in Account; moves domains, certificates and initial installation to Environment; reserves console assignments for unassigned Access; and assigns Account catalog registration to Registeel. The configuration-bundle design assigns the shared Transform/Connect/System configuration installer and its service installation/update to Deploy, and each target API and payload semantics to its existing product pair. Use configuration bundles in guidance and CONFIGURATION in bundle/component types; migrate legacy DATA contracts across Build, Marketplace and Deploy. Use a synthetic configuration integration for installer acceptance, without adding a Model pilot or a new product owner.

products.name: Documentation
products.summary: Documentation publishes product documentation and serves a configurable developer portal with API references, guides and interactive examples.
notes: Added by explicit user request on 2026-10-07 after review of site-tech-ui and documentation; no spreadsheet row is claimed. Documentation is the canonical product name, not an alias for Site or Document.

Unown builds the reusable publishing API and developer portal; Togetic configures existing capabilities. Require apply-engineering-guidelines and build-frontend-backends with React, strict TypeScript and tRPC. Historical sources describe behavior, not the approved implementation stack or a verified deployment.

The reviewed UI depends on a separate site-tech-api absent from the supplied projects. Discover and verify that contract before claiming integration. Preserve Account, Model, Console, Build, Marketplace, Environment and Deploy ownership.

products.name: Account
products.summary: Account manages Prism identities and keys, guides Prism-managed or client-owned AWS setup, creates or adopts the backing account, verifies Prism service access and emits bootstrap manifests.
notes: Added by explicit user request after the supplied spreadsheet; no source row is claimed. Kangaskhan builds the Account API; Blissey guides and configures existing deployments.

Account owns identity, keys, the AWS account record, explicit create-or-adopt provisioning, Prism cross-account service readiness and bootstrap-manifest output. Its configurer also guides a client through standalone AWS signup before using the same existing-account adoption path. It does not own domains, certificates, initial platform installation, customer console assignments or Prism Marketplace registration.

products.name: Access
products.summary: Access will own IAM Identity Center and customer AWS Console assignments.
notes: Account onboarding identifies this as an ownership gap. Do not implement temporary customer console users or Identity Center assignments inside Account.

products.name: Console
products.summary: Console renders reusable authenticated applications from governed, versioned UI configurations.
notes: Assigned by explicit user request on 2026-10-06. Chandelure builds the reusable Console runtime and configuration API; Vivillon configures applications on existing deployments. Console configuration is an artifact, not a separate product. Keep Model composition, Persist facts, Account identity and System execution with their owning products.

products.name: Environment
products.summary: Environment prepares tenant environments, shared routing and initial product installations.
notes: Torterra builds Environment; Shaymin configures existing deployments. Bootstrap is its setup adapter, including the initial no-service install path. HTTP API capabilities are required build scope, not a claim that a service is already deployed.
Environment bootstraps the Deploy run service and installs its Deploy-owned Puller component; ongoing subscriber behavior belongs to Corviknight/Skarmory.

products.name: Marketplace
products.summary: Marketplace catalogs products and reviews, publishes and rolls back bundles.
notes: Regigigas builds Marketplace catalog/publication capabilities. Deploy owns Puller subscriptions, polling, installation history and update execution. Marketplace supplies its supported catalog/publication interfaces; verify notification support rather than restoring historical subscription APIs.

Register, review and publish configuration bundles using the CONFIGURATION component type; migrate legacy catalog metadata and publication contracts. Require compatible shared Deploy provider and configuration API prerequisites in review environments; catalog rollback does not reverse applied configuration.

products.name: Build
products.summary: Build turns validated source into portable deployment artifacts with provenance.
notes: Tinkaton builds the Build API and runner; Metang configures build jobs. Build provenance does not imply Marketplace publication or Deploy completion.

Build configuration bundles as portable CDK assemblies containing configuration assets and declarations referencing the shared Deploy provider. Use CONFIGURATION consistently in request, artifact and provenance schemas; validate payload digests and provider contract requirements without executing configuration APIs during builds.

products.name: Deploy
products.summary: Deploy installs products and configuration bundles through a shared installer and keeps subscribed components updated.
notes: Corviknight builds Deploy, including its Puller subscriber component; Skarmory configures runs, subscriptions, polling, update policy and recovery. Keep subscriber desired state, install history and subscription secrets in the Deploy-owned Puller component, separate from the stateless SigV4 run API. Separate packages or stacks do not create a separate product.

Own the shared configuration-bundle installer and typed Transform, Connect and System API adapters. Ship the provider as part of Deploy service infrastructure through its normal installation/update lifecycle. Reuse a provider per target account/region across bundle stacks; do not package a custom Lambda per bundle. Keep operation receipts separate from Puller subscriber state. Use configuration bundles and the CONFIGURATION type consistently; migrate legacy type handling and subscription metadata with Build and Marketplace. Follow skills/build-product-deployer/reference/configuration-bundles.md.

products.name: Model
products.summary: Model governs vocabulary, definitions and compatible artifact releases.
notes: Merge spreadsheet rows 34 and 57 into one Model product. Dialga builds Model; Jirachi configures existing APIs and governed releases. Preserve Lexicon artifact contracts and Mew as a retained modeling specialist; API assignment does not establish runtime availability.

products.name: Transform
products.summary: Transform converts registered source languages into target languages and extracts schema-validated JSON from strings using configured Bedrock models.
notes: Resolve the spreadsheet test-only/configuration mismatch: Silvally authors and tests mappings; Kecleon owns engine implementation. Preserve test-only intent when the user only requests evaluation.

Own validation, immutable/versioned registration, read-back and lifecycle semantics for Transform configuration consumed by the shared Deploy installer. Kecleon handles API gaps; Silvally authors and validates mapping payloads under its existing readiness gates. Do not create per-bundle installer code.

Add non-deterministic extraction as a distinct Transform phase: immutable configuration selects an Amazon Bedrock model, extraction instructions and an output JSON Schema; a TypeScript worker uses the AI SDK to extract validated structured JSON from string input. Kecleon implements the versioned API/runtime capability; Silvally configures it only after deployed support is verified. Preserve the existing Spark SQL contract and production-derived mapping readiness gates. Follow skills/build-transform-product/reference/non-deterministic-extraction.md.

products.name: Persist
products.summary: Persist ingests and queries graph facts, maintains derived indexes and triggers, and owns lexicon-governed vector search composed through GraphQL.
notes: User override: retain Conkeldurr for Persist only. Uxie configures existing deployments.

Requested 2026-10-05: keep embeddings, OpenSearch vector indexing and GraphQL search composition in a separate vector-search feature piece. Model owns lexicon field eligibility; Persist owns implementation and GraphQL source routing. This scope assignment does not establish deployed support.

products.name: Rule
products.summary: Rule selects entities and evaluates governed predicates.

products.name: Connect
products.summary: Connect exchanges files and requests with external partners.
notes: Own flow, partner-configuration and activation API lifecycle semantics consumed by the shared Deploy installer. Lapras handles API gaps; Wingull authors and verifies payloads and secret references. Configuration registration must not implicitly start partner jobs.

products.name: System
products.summary: System orchestrates business outcomes through reusable configured flows.
notes: User override: Zygarde builds System; Celebi configures outcomes. Current scope is the orchestration core, not all historical Product features.

Own definition, template, flow and waterfall configuration API lifecycle semantics consumed by the shared Deploy installer. Zygarde handles API gaps; Celebi composes configurations with pinned leaf references. Registering a configuration bundle must not implicitly invoke a business flow.
